cultural.vision_reason: This shows a hand-woven strip-cloth waist-cloth with indigo tie-dye resist patterning, a well-documented Tiv textile tradition (the diamond/lozenge motif is characteristic of Tiv indigo-dyed cloths like the "anger" and related weaves).

physical.title: cloth; waist-cloth
physical.summary: Cloth (an open-mesh sash or waist-cloth), composed of 10 strips of hand-spun cotton sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are identical, each being woven from alternating stripes of natural and indigo-dyed  cotton, with the warp threads bunched towards the edges and loosely separated down the middle; the indigo weft is also widely spaced so that the warp and weft together create an open mesh. The cloth after being assembled was tied and dyed in indigo; this has produced a bold pattern of a central circle of undyed cloth with extensions at the four corners, set against an indigo background. The warp ends have been knotted to form a fringe.
